content:
Due to the fact that lean4 is newer than some of the older languages like Coq and Isabelle. We are missing on a lot of theorems that have been proved before. I understand that mathlib is being worked on, but in the meantime, it would be nice if there was some sort of integration method.

For example, consider a theorem proved in isabelle, I would like to connect its results to lean.. now the only way i can think of it right now is that you would do the prove in isabelle but then you would set it as an axiom in lean, but that's disconnected and not couplled, which can lead to problems in the future

It's an interesting idea, but quite hard to match things up in practice. For example, each has their own development of the real numbers. Do you take it as an axiom that they match identically, or do you first build some kind of formally verified translation between them?

Interoperability of proof systems is a central goal of the Dedukti project which aims to connect Isabelle/HOL, HOL Light, Lean and Rocq among others.
There is also this project: https://www.renaissancephilanthropy.org/leaning-and-rocqing
And there was the work of "Theorem" on translating software foundations from Rocq to Lean and back: https://theorem.dev/blog/lf-lean/
